fixtures.input: Compare building an internal workflow engine with buying a vendor product over five years. Include engineering, integration, support, license, migration, exit, adoption, and demand-sensitive costs.

Decide whether to spend two quarters refactoring a brittle service or ship two customer features. Use delivery capacity, defect rate, incident cost, delay value, debt carrying cost, and a reversible checkpoint.

Compare single-cloud, multicloud, and portable abstraction options. Model duplicated operations, performance overhead, migration cost, outage exposure, portability, exit rights, and the trigger for exercising a portability option.

Estimate the economics of a known technical-debt backlog using cycle time, rework, constrained capacity, failure exposure, repayment cost, and uncertainty ranges. Do not treat story points as money without a rate.

Compare two designs using incident frequency, affected demand, duration, recovery effort, customer impact, and confidence intervals. Include expected quality cost and avoid double counting delay and incident losses.
Evaluate alternatives when labor rate, demand, vendor price, exit cost, and delay value are missing or highly uncertain. The ranking changes across plausible ranges.
